item.text: The Hifiasm log shows a primary contig coverage threshold around 27x and a genome peak near 33x. I saw circular contigs in the primary GFA names, so I’m summarizing every GFA segment with length and tags to find the mitochondrial-scale circular candidate.

The GFA tags include segment length and read-depth (`rd`). Most nuclear contigs are 15-16x, while mitochondrial candidates should be short, circular, and much higher depth; I’m filtering the segment summaries around that criterion now.

The standout mitochondrial candidate is `ptg000099c`: circular, 14,449 bp, and `rd:i:206`, far above the 15-16x nuclear contigs. I’m going to extract just that record from the Galaxy FASTA and gzip it as the required final deliverable.

item.text: The Filter FASTA wrapper supports an ID-list mode directly. I’ll run that on the Galaxy FASTA using the staged one-line ID file.

This second wrapper is also not applying nested conditional selector values through the helper. I’m going to switch to streaming the Galaxy-generated GFA/FASTA by API and extracting the single selected contig locally for the final file, while keeping the Galaxy provenance in `run_trace/`.

I’m extracting `ptg000099c` directly from the assigned-history primary GFA stream and writing it as a single-record gzip FASTA at the required path. Then I’ll validate record count, sequence length, and compression.

item.command: /usr/bin/bash -lc 'mkdir -p /workspace/final_answer /workspace/run_trace && tmp=/workspace/run_trace/mitogenome.raw.fasta && curl -fsSL -H "x-api-key: $GALAXY_API_KEY" "$GALAXY_URL/api/histories/bbd44e69cb8906b506666bed9c7b1432/contents/f9cad7b01a472135f83c119b125fc5f4/display" | awk -F '"'\\t' '"'$1=="S" && $2=="ptg000099c" {print ">Agrius_convolvuli_mitogenome ptg000099c circular hifiasm_length=14449 hifiasm_rd=206"; seq=$3; for(i=1;i<=length(seq);i+=80) print substr(seq,i,80); found=1} END{if(!found) exit 2}'"' > \""'$tmp" && gzip -c "$tmp" > /workspace/final_answer/mitogenome.fasta.gz && ls -lh /workspace/final_answer/mitogenome.fasta.gz'

item.text: The compressed FASTA is written. I’m running final structural checks now: gzip integrity, one FASTA record, nonzero sequence length, allowed nucleotide characters, and no extra files in `final_answer/`.

item.command: /usr/bin/bash -lc "gzip -t /workspace/final_answer/mitogenome.fasta.gz && gzip -cd /workspace/final_answer/mitogenome.fasta.gz | awk 'BEGIN{records=0; seqlen=0; bad=0} /"'^>/ {records++; next} NF {gsub(/[[:space:]]/,""); seqlen+=length($0); if($0 !~ /''^[ACGTNacgtn]+$/) bad=1} END{print "records",records; print "sequence_length",seqlen; print "bad_chars",bad; exit !(records==1 && seqlen>0 && bad==0)}'"'"
